english.title: Procure broadcast from prescribed areas of high seas capable of being received in UK
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) procured a broadcast to be made that was capable of being received in the United Kingdom from a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), which was not British-registered, while it was within a prescribed area of the high seas
english.legislation: Contrary to section 79(1)(a) and (3) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that proceedings in England and Wales for this offence may be brought only by OFCOM or by or with the consent of the Secretary of State or the DPP.
(ii) Section 79(4) of the Act provides that the making of a broadcast does not contravene section 79(1) if it is shown to have been authorised under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.
(iii) Section 79(5) of the Act provides that prescribed means prescribed for the purposes of this section by an order made by the Secretary of State.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(v) Section 94 of the Act provides a saving for broadcasts made under and in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence.
(vi) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011, (In force 01/10/2011), introduces a £100-00p fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act, as from that date. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Fixed Penalty charge of £100-00p (in force from 01/10/2011).

For offences committed before the commencement of section 282(3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003:
Six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
